Lower band (1-2): Limited knowledge, e.g. ‘they should use job production because it makes one product at a time’.
Mid band (3-5): Accurate analysis with some application, e.g. ‘job production allows each motorcycle to be built to the customer’s exact specifications, using skilled craftspeople. This means the manufacturer can charge premium prices, increasing profit margins.’
Top band (6-9): Detailed justified recommendation with evaluation of alternatives, e.g. ‘the motorcycle manufacturer should use job production because each customer wants a unique motorcycle built to their specifications. Therefore, job production is the most appropriate choice for a business making unique, high-value products.’

expect:
Lower band (1-2): Identifies advantages/disadvantages of JIT with limited understanding.
Mid band (3-5): Explains advantages and disadvantages with some application and analysis. E.g. JIT reduces warehouse costs, improving profitability; however, late deliveries can halt production.
Top band (6-9): Detailed, balanced analysis leading to a justified recommendation.
Possible content:
• For: JIT eliminates warehouse costs (rent, electricity, staff, security), improves cash flow, and reduces waste from expired or damaged stock. This means the business can pass savings on to customers or increase profit margins.
• Against: JIT requires extremely reliable suppliers. If a single delivery is late, the entire production line stops. The business also loses economies of scale from bulk purchasing, increasing variable costs per unit.
• Judgement: It depends on the type of business — a manufacturer with reliable, nearby suppliers (e.g. Toyota) benefits greatly, but a business with long international supply chains faces higher risk of disruption.

Understanding (up to 3 marks):

Application (up to 3 marks):
• Last Course Patisserie makes hand-made desserts fresh to order (1). The new chef from Switzerland has introduced new products, increasing demand (1). Implementing QA could maintain quality standards as the business expands to new premises (1).
